Forest clearing is connected to lost food and breeding sites; roots and sediment explain downstream effects. Conservation teaching matches threats to actions. Evaluation compares goal, legal limits, evidence, costs, and avoided damage.

Renewable resources require time and suitable conditions. Breeding needs approval and a safe release habitat. Conservation can allow lawful use; protected areas have specific rules. The road comparison explicitly controls other environmental effects and warns against universalizing that choice.
